question.context: A sign-in from an anonymous IP address `95.202.65.202` was detected, which might indicate use of Tor browser or anonymizer VPNs. This is part of a larger security incident involving multiple alerts, one of which is a BEC financial fraud attempt wherein a suspicious inbox rule was created during a risky Azure Active Directory session.
question.question: Can you identify the Security Identifier (SID) of the account associated with the suspicious activity that created the inbox rule?
solution: The user with AadUserId `89e933b9-5b2e-4bd6-bcdf-033db707ef82` signed in from an anonymous IP address.

A suspicious inbox rule was created in a risky Azure Active Directory session, associated with the user account having SID `S-1-5-21-1740051960-3534030288-108486866-1602`, indicating a potential business email compromise (BEC) financial fraud attempt.

SELECT TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, UserId, UserDisplayName, IsRisky, RiskLevelAggregated, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskState
FROM env_monitor_db.SigninLogs
WHERE IPAddress = '95.202.65.202'
ORDER BY TimeGenerated DESC
LIMIT 20

SELECT TimeGenerated,
       Operation,
       UserId,
       MailboxOwnerUPN,
       MailboxOwnerSid,
       LogonUserSid,
       LogonUserDisplayName,
       Parameters
FROM env_monitor_db.OfficeActivity
WHERE Operation LIKE '%InboxRule%'
  AND TimeGenerated BETWEEN '2024-07-22 08:40:00' AND '2024-07-22 09:00:00'
  AND (MailboxOwnerUPN = 'laylaw@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co'
       OR UserId = 'laylaw@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co'
       OR MailboxOwnerUPN IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY TimeGenerated ASC
LIMIT 50

SELECT TimeGenerated,
       Operation,
       Activity,
       UserId,
       MailboxOwnerUPN,
       MailboxOwnerSid,
       LogonUserSid,
       LogonUserDisplayName,
       ClientIP,
       Client_IPAddress
FROM env_monitor_db.OfficeActivity
WHERE TimeGenerated BETWEEN '2024-07-22 08:40:00' AND '2024-07-22 09:00:00'
  AND (
       ClientIP = '95.202.65.202'
       OR Client_IPAddress = '95.202.65.202'
      )
ORDER BY TimeGenerated ASC
LIMIT 100

SELECT TimeGenerated,
       IncidentName,
       Title,
       Description,
       Severity,
       Status,
       AlertIds
FROM env_monitor_db.SecurityIncident
WHERE (Title LIKE '%business email compromise%'
    OR Title LIKE '%BEC%'
    OR Title LIKE '%inbox rule%'
    OR Description LIKE '%business email compromise%'
    OR Description LIKE '%BEC%'
    OR Description LIKE '%inbox rule%'
    OR Title LIKE '%financial fraud%'
    OR Description LIKE '%financial fraud%')
ORDER BY TimeGenerated DESC
LIMIT 20

SELECT TimeGenerated,
       AlertId,
       AlertName,
       DisplayName,
       Description,
       AlertSeverity,
       ProviderName,
       VendorName
FROM env_monitor_db.SecurityAlert
WHERE AlertName LIKE '%business email compromise%'
   OR AlertName LIKE '%BEC%'
   OR AlertName LIKE '%inbox rule%'
   OR AlertName LIKE '%inbox rules%'
   OR AlertName LIKE '%financial fraud%'
   OR Description LIKE '%business email compromise%'
   OR Description LIKE '%BEC%'
   OR Description LIKE '%inbox rule%'
   OR Description LIKE '%financial fraud%'
ORDER BY TimeGenerated DESC
LIMIT 50

This may indicate that the user account is compromised, and the mailbox is being used for spreading phishing emails or gaining access to other accounts and devices.

question.context: An alert was generated indicating that an inbound rule was created to hide incoming emails potentially as part of a business email compromise (BEC) fraud attempt. The account involved was Jordan P associated with email `Jordan P@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` and originating from IP `255.246.85.58`. The incident took place during a risky Azure Active Directory session.
question.question: Which cloud application (AppId) was involved in the incident where the user Jordan P had a suspicious inbox manipulation rule?
solution: A suspicious inbox manipulation rule was set on the inbox of the user Jordan P (laylaw@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co), indicating a potential compromise. A MoveToFolder rule named ITCleanup was created to move messages to a folder named RSS Feeds.

A suspicious inbox rule that hides incoming email messages was created in a risky Azure Active Directory session. It indicates a potential attempt at business email compromise (BEC) targeting the email account Jordan P@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co.

SELECT 
  i.IncidentNumber,
  i.Title,
  i.Description,
  i.AlertIds
FROM SecurityIncident i
WHERE 
  i.Title LIKE '%Business Email Compromise%' 
  OR i.Title LIKE '%BEC%' 
  OR i.Description LIKE '%Business Email Compromise%' 
  OR i.Description LIKE '%BEC%'
ORDER BY i.CreatedTime DESC
LIMIT 10

SELECT 
  SystemAlertId,
  AlertName,
  Description,
  CompromisedEntity,
  TimeGenerated
FROM SecurityAlert
WHERE 
  AlertName LIKE '%Business Email Compromise%'
  OR AlertName LIKE '%BEC%'
  OR Description LIKE '%Business Email Compromise%'
  OR Description LIKE '%BEC%'
ORDER BY TimeGenerated DESC
LIMIT 20

SELECT 
  'Alert' AS SourceTable,
  AlertId,
  AlertName,
  AlertDescription,
  AlertContext,
  TimeGenerated
FROM Alert
WHERE 
  AlertName LIKE '%Business Email%'
  OR AlertName LIKE '%Business Email Compromise%'
  OR AlertName LIKE '%BEC%'
  OR AlertDescription LIKE '%Business Email%'
  OR AlertDescription LIKE '%Business Email Compromise%'
  OR AlertDescription LIKE '%BEC%'
  OR AlertDescription LIKE '%inbox rule%'
  OR AlertDescription LIKE '%financial fraud%'
  OR AlertContext LIKE '%Business Email%'
  OR AlertContext LIKE '%Business Email Compromise%'
  OR AlertContext LIKE '%BEC%'
  OR AlertContext LIKE '%inbox rule%'
  OR AlertContext LIKE '%financial fraud%'

  Title AS AlertName,

question.context: During a multi-stage security incident, an alert was triggered related to a suspicious inbox manipulation rule set on the inbox of the user Jordan P (laylaw@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co). The rule named ITCleanup moved messages to a folder named RSS Feeds, which may indicate account compromise and potential use for spreading phishing emails or gaining access to other accounts and devices.
question.question: What is the Azure Active Directory User ID (AadUserId) of the account involved in the financial fraud attempt detected through a suspicious inbox rule in a risky session?
solution: A suspicious inbox rule named ITCleanup was set by the account with AadUserId `89e933b9-5b2e-4bd6-bcdf-033db707ef82`, which belongs to user `Jordan P (laylaw@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co)`, to move messages to a folder named RSS Feeds.

A suspicious inbox rule that hides incoming email messages was also created by the same account with AadUserId `89e933b9-5b2e-4bd6-bcdf-033db707ef82`, which may indicate an attempted business email compromise (BEC) financial fraud.

This security threat indicates that an attacker might have hijacked this user's account to sift through sensitive financial data in SAP for potential misuse. The alert was triggered by a risky sign-in detected in Microsoft Entra ID, which could be indicative of compromised credentials or an unauthorized access attempt.
question.question: Can you identify the IP address from which the suspicious sign-in to SAP was made?
solution: A suspicious SAP authentication was detected from IP address `107.253.5.27`. This indicates that a user account with a risky sign-in alert in Microsoft Entra ID accessed SAP, potentially to record or modify sensitive financial information.

trajectory.action:
SELECT DISTINCT IPAddress, IsAnonymousProxy, IPCategory, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, Application, TimeGenerated
FROM CloudAppEvents
WHERE Application LIKE '%SAP%'
  AND (
        AccountDisplayName LIKE 'Jordan P%' 
        OR AccountId LIKE '%Jordan P@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co%'
        OR AccountId LIKE '%jordan p@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co%'
      )
  AND (
        IsAnonymousProxy = 'True'
        OR IsAnonymousProxy = '1'
        OR IPCategory LIKE '%anonymous%'
      )
ORDER BY TimeGenerated DESC
LIMIT 10

SELECT 
  UserDisplayName,
  UserPrincipalName,
  RiskEventType,
  IpAddress,
  DetectedDateTime,
  RiskDetail,
  RiskLevel,
  RiskState
FROM AADUserRiskEvents
WHERE 
  (UserPrincipalName LIKE '%Jordan P@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co%'
   OR UserDisplayName LIKE 'Jordan P%')
  AND RiskEventType LIKE '%anonymous%'
ORDER BY DetectedDateTime DESC
LIMIT 10

SELECT 
  TimeGenerated,
  UserDisplayName,
  UserPrincipalName,
  IsRisky,
  RiskEventTypes,
  RiskEventTypes_V2,
  IPAddress
FROM SigninLogs
WHERE 
  (UserPrincipalName LIKE '%Jordan P@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co%'
   OR UserDisplayName LIKE 'Jordan P%')
  AND (IsRisky = 'True' OR IsRisky = '1')
  AND (
        RiskEventTypes LIKE '%anonymous%' 
        OR RiskEventTypes_V2 LIKE '%anonymous%'
      )
ORDER BY TimeGenerated DESC
LIMIT 10

SELECT 
  a.TimeGenerated,
  a.DisplayName,
  a.Description,
  a.AlertName,
  a.AlertType,
  a.AlertSeverity,
  a.Entities
FROM SecurityAlert a
WHERE 
  a.Description LIKE '%Jordan P%'
   OR a.Description LIKE '%Jordan P@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co%'
   OR a.DisplayName LIKE '%Jordan P%'
   OR a.AlertName LIKE '%SAP%'
   OR a.Description LIKE '%SAP%'
ORDER BY a.TimeGenerated DESC
LIMIT 20

question.context: A multi-stage security incident involving BEC (business email compromise) and financial fraud occurred in our organization. The incident began when a suspicious inbox rule that hides incoming email messages was created in a risky Azure Active Directory session by the user account of Jordan P with email `Jordan P@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` and IP address `255.246.85.58`. This indicates an attempt to conduct a BEC attack.
question.question: Which mailbox primary address was involved in sending suspicious emails related to the ongoing BEC fraud attempt?

Suspicious emails related to a BEC (business email compromise) fraud attempt were sent from the mailbox with the primary address `tony@avoriaz.alpineskihouse.co`.
